answer: Sequential work counter. Each identity must solve a randomly ordered chain of small computational puzzles whose answers feed the next step; progress is checkpointed to a shared vault that verifies continuity, so parallel identities cannot pool results without duplicating the full chain. Registration also requires a distinctive opal-tagged hardware token issued once per device. To run N identities, an attacker must buy N tokens and dedicate N serial compute streams, since skipping steps breaks the chain and the river of verified progress rejects the submission.
